ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the rhombus $ABCD$, diagonal $AC=8$, $BD=10$, then what is the area of $\triangle ADO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In diamond $ABCD$, the diagonals have lengths $AC=8$ and $BD=10$,\\
$\therefore$OA=4, OD=5, and $AC\perp BD$,\\
$\therefore$the area of $\triangle ADO$ is $\frac{1}{2}OA\cdot OD=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 5=\boxed{10}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: ABCD is drawn as a diamond-shaped rhombus with A at the top, C at the bottom, B left, D right, and diagonals AC and BD crossing at O; triangle ADO is the upper-right small triangle formed by the two diagonals and side AD. From the text, take AC = 8 and BD = 10. Use the rhombus area formula: area(ABCD) = (AC × BD)/2 = (8 × 10)/2 = 40. Since the diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other and split the rhombus into four congruent/equal-area triangles, triangle ADO has one-fourth of the rhombus area: 40/4 = 10.
